articles.title: 'Threatened with acid attack': Delhi woman drugged, raped on pretext of job offer
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A 41-year-old woman was allegedly drugged and raped on the pretext of a job opportunity in east Delhi’s Mandawali area, and later blackmailed
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A 41-year-old woman was allegedly drugged and raped on the pretext of a job opportunity in east Delhi’s Mandawali area, and later blackmailed with a purported video of the incident, police said on Thursday.Police have registered a case in connection with the incident and are conducting raids to apprehend the accused, who is currently absconding, they added.According to news agency PTI, the woman, a resident of Laxmi Nagar, alleged that the accused, Deepak Bansal of Ganesh Nagar, had befriended her around two years ago and promised to help her secure a job.According to the complaint, Bansal approached the woman on March 4 on the pretext of discussing a job and allegedly gave her a substance that rendered her unconscious. He then allegedly raped her, police said.After regaining consciousness, the woman objected to the alleged assault. Bansal then allegedly threatened to circulate a purported video of the incident on social media, police said.The woman also alleged that the accused took her gold bangles, ring and chain and threatened her with dire consequences if she reported the matter to the police.According to the complaint, the accused claimed to have contacts in the police and threatened to throw acid on the woman if she reported the incident.The woman remained silent for several months due to fear but later approached police after allegedly facing continued harassment from the accused.Police said a case was registered against Bansal at Mandawali police station on September 22 under relevant provisions.Teams are conducting raids at possible locations to trace and apprehend the accused, who is currently absconding.The woman has been provided counselling, they said.(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Meta unveils camera-free Ray-Ban Audio glasses and a keychain AI companion at Connect 2026
articles.summary: At its annual Meta Connect event, Facebook-parent Meta has announced a major expansion of its consumer hardware portfolio with the launch of new Ray-Ban
articles.body: At its annual Meta Connect event, Facebook-parent Meta has announced a major expansion of its consumer hardware portfolio with the launch of new Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses and a quirky Muse AI keychain. The new products unveiled highlight Meta’s AI push to embed AI agents into everyday life simply by blending fashion, utility and entertainment. The new Ray-Ban Meta glasses lineup builds on Meta’s partnership with EssilorLuxottica. The glasses now feature deeper AI integration, including voice-controlled access to Meta’s AI assistant, improved audio quality, and enhanced camera capabilities. On the other hand, Meta Muse AI keychain is a pocket-sized device described as “Tamagotchi-like.” The gadget acts as a portable AI agent, offering playful interactions, reminders, and personalized assistance. Meta positioned Muse as a way to make AI more approachable, turning everyday tasks into engaging experiences.Ray-Ban Meta Audio: cameras out, all-day wearability inThe headline hardware announcement was Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Meta's first-ever camera-free smart glasses, developed through its ongoing partnership with EssilorLuxottica. By ditching the camera setup entirely, Meta managed to bring the glasses down to just 43 grams — noticeably lighter than the roughly 50g standard Ray-Ban Meta models and far lighter than the 70g Display glasses — while still packing in hands-free music and podcast playback, calling, and conversations with Meta's AI assistant. The glasses come in Clubmaster and Burbank styles, with customizable temple tips, nose pads, and overextension hinges for a more tailored fit, and support a wide range of optical prescriptions.Battery life is rated at up to 12 hours on a single charge, extendable to roughly 48 additional hours using the included charging case. Ray-Ban Meta Audio launches October 13 at $349, with pre-orders open now.Meta also used the moment to introduce Hearing Enhancement, an FDA-cleared accessibility feature arriving later this year for supported AI glasses. Using the glasses' six-speaker array, the feature is designed to help people who are hard of hearing pick out speech more clearly in noisy environments, letting users adjust left-right audio balance or shift to mono audio in one ear. Meta is pricing it at $149.99 as a one-time purchase, or bundling it into a Meta One subscription, framing it as a notably more affordable alternative to traditional hearing aids, which the company says typically start around $800. A 30-day free trial will also be available.Beyond the audio-only model, Meta also refreshed its standard Ray-Ban Meta line with the Gen 3 glasses, adding a slimmer build, longer battery life, a 12MP camera, and 3K Ultra HD video recording. The company additionally previewed a new hologram calling feature for Ray-Ban Meta Display users, letting someone do a quick self-capture with their phone to generate a hologram visible to whoever they're calling — expected to arrive in early access on WhatsApp in the US within the next few months.Muse Charm: an AI agent you can put on a keychainThe event's true "one more thing" moment came when CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled Muse Charm, a small, palm-sized wearable designed to give people another physical way to interact with Muse, Meta's recently launched and increasingly popular personal AI agent.The device houses a tiny screen displaying Jolly, the cute animated avatar Meta has built to represent Muse, and is meant to be carried in a pocket or clipped onto a keychain. Zuckerberg explained that the team condensed the entire Muse experience — including its real-time voice and avatar system — into a device small enough to live on a keychain while remaining constantly available to talk to. A fingerprint sensor built into the corner of the device lets users start a conversation instantly, without needing to unlock a phone or open an app first. For anyone not wearing AI glasses, Zuckerberg positioned Muse Charm as the fastest possible way to talk to Muse and show it what's happening around you.The gadget leans into a distinctly Tamagotchi-like aesthetic — small, personality-driven, and designed to keep users continually engaged with Meta's AI software. Zuckerberg acknowledged the hardware isn't quite ready for release, saying the team still needs to finalize how its internal components are laid out, but confirmed Muse Charm is on track to ship in time for the December holiday season.You use AI every day. articles.title: A $12,055 library bill was waived after a New Hampshire man returned an 1894 magazine that had been overdue for 48,220 days, or 132 years
articles.summary: John Hanson walked into the Concord Public Library in New Hampshire with a September 1894 issue of The Century Illustrated Monthly Magazine.
articles.body: John Hanson walked into the Concord Public Library in New Hampshire with a September 1894 issue of The Century Illustrated Monthly Magazine. The 84-year-old Barrington resident had kept the magazine for decades, and when he returned it in September 2026, the item was 48,220 days overdue. That would have amounted to a $12,055 penalty under the library’s previous fine system, but he did not have to pay it because the library had begun a year-long freeze on overdue fines.The magazine had been sitting in his homeHanson told library staff that he did not know exactly how the magazine ended up in his possession; it had been in his home for years before he decided to return it after learning about Concord Public Library’s new fine-free policy. The item was a September 1894 issue of The Century Illustrated Monthly Magazine, which was a publication that was already more than a century old when Hanson brought it back. FOX 5 reported that the magazine had been 48,220 days overdue according to the library’s calculation.Concord Public Library had announced that beginning September 1, 2026, it would freeze fines for 12 months while the city evaluated the effects of moving toward a fine-free system. Under the policy, existing fines were frozen and patrons would no longer accumulate overdue charges for ordinary late returns. Hanson’s return therefore came during a period when the library was actively encouraging people to bring back overdue materials without getting worried about accumulated penalties.The fine was theoretical, not a bill he had to payThe $12,055 figure represents what the late fee would have been under the calculation reported by the library, and Hanson did not actually receive a $12,055 bill when he returned the magazine. FOX 5 reported that the library had expected overdue materials to come back during the fine freeze but did not expect something from the late 19th century to turn up. The magazine was not returned to normal circulation because of its age, and library staff said that it could instead be preserved in the Concord Room.Concord said that its year-long experiment would allow officials to evaluate what happens when overdue fines are removed as a barrier to returning materials. The freeze covers current fines for 12 months, although the library retains restrictions for lost or damaged items and certain overdue accounts.The case also shows us how a policy that is designed to encourage ordinary overdue returns can produce unexpected results when an item has been missing for generations. Staff could now treat its return as an opportunity to preserve an unusual piece of the library’s collection history instead of treating the magazine simply as a long-overdue loan.What happens to the 1894 issue nowUPI reported that library officials said it would not be returned to circulation and could instead be displayed in the building’s Concord Room, which gives the returned issue a different status from an ordinary overdue item. It has become an archival object that is connected to the library’s own history, complete with evidence of its original circulation.The episode also illustrates why the library’s fine-free experiment matters in practical terms, since Hanson said that he decided to return the magazine after hearing about the freeze, and the library received an item that had been missing since the 19th century. For Concord Public Library, the September 1894 issue came back in its possession, 48,220 days after its due date, and the $12,055 theoretical fine did not have to be paid.You use AI every day. articles.title: In England, a retired man spent 30 years building a slate miniature Lake District village, then moved the handmade town to hotel grounds so the public could see it
articles.summary: Discover the incredible journey of a retired builder who spent three decades crafting a slate miniature village of the Lake District, now relocated to a hotel for public enjoyment.
articles.body: Some pastimes remain modest. Others gradually gain control of a garden, then a reputation, and ultimately require a brand-new house. A retired builder, Robinson, in the Lake District town of Flookburgh worked on a project for thirty years that developed from a hobby into a legitimate tourist destination. When the project's initial location eventually closed, it had to be meticulously dismantled and reconstructed somewhere else.A retired Cumbria builder spent nearly 30 years building a miniature representation of the Lake District, using slate almost exclusively from the local area. Each building might take up to six months to construct, pieced together from the same stone as the real farmhouses and cottages strewn throughout the surrounding fells. As the attraction states on the Damson Dene Hotel, 'What started as a method to fill his retirement evolved to about a hundred slate models, up to a metre high, laid out in the yard of his own home and attracting thousands of tourists a year.'Robinson had first worked with limestone but switched to slate, a medium that drew him in more, even if it was unforgiving. Working with it required special attention, as one error could shatter months of labour. Robinson has observed that you have to bite your tongue when you feel like swearing, a line that conveys the quiet persistence behind such a tedious hobby.Robinson and his wife, in 2021, chose to close the original display, hoping someone else may take it on, rather than let decades of work go into storage. Finally a South Cumbria hotelier accepted the call and offered the grounds of one of his hotels as a permanent new site for the collection.Shifting a village stone by stoneMoving some hundred hand-built slate buildings was still no small undertaking, even though Robinson had built each one with eventual transport in mind, which made the physical move itself manageable. The real challenge was reassembly: it fell to a local builder to painstakingly recreate the whole village on fresh ground, a job that took about a year and demanded tremendous care to get right on unfamiliar terrain. Today the village sits adjacent to Bowness-on-Windermere, with the Lyth Valley in the background.In its new home, the collection includes tiny replicas of some of the region's best-known landmarks, among them the Bridge House in Ambleside, Townend Farmhouse at Troutbeck and Slaters Bridge in Little Langdale. Perhaps the most notable inclusion is a small-scale recreation of Hill Top, the seventeenth-century farmhouse near Sawrey that originally belonged to the novelist and illustrator Beatrix Potter, now cared for as one of the National Trust’s most visited literary assets.A literary garden for a literary villageThe model buildings now sit with their life-sized bronze sculptures of Beatrix Potter and the writer John Ruskin, seated with her in calm conversation on a bench. The pair, created by Lancaster-based sculptor and Fellow of the Royal Society of Sculptors Alan Ward, who works from a studio at Lancaster Castle, provides a human-scale counterpart to the miniature world around it and connects the display more closely to the literary history of the wider Lake District.Now the layout presents a little twist for the visitor: an opportunity to walk among miniature versions of structures he may later visit full-size before lunch or a swim at the hotel itself. The attraction is open 365 days a year and admittance tokens can be purchased at the hotel reception. What’s particularly striking about the story isn’t so much the size of the buildings themselves but the tenacity behind them. Thirty years of painstaking, repetitive craftsmanship, made entirely by hand from a tough local stone, could easily have ended up in a skip or a storage unit when the original site closed. Instead, thanks to Robinson's own patience and a hotelier's willingness to take on an unconventional project, his slate townships continue to greet visitors, just a short drive from the real landscapes they were built to imitate.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2015, a Minnesota couple entered the Boundary Waters to oppose a proposed mine; 366 days and 2,000 miles later, they emerged without crossing a road or entering a building
articles.summary: In a remarkable display of environmental activism, Dave and Amy Freeman spent an entire year in Minnesota's Boundary Waters without crossing a road or entering a building, raising awareness against proposed mining activities that threaten the watershed.
articles.body: On rare occasions, activists decide to use their presence as a point of contention, remaining in the area they wish to be protected for so long that it is impossible to ignore. This was the motivation behind one of the more unusual protest trips of the past ten years, which was conducted solely by foot, kayak, and ski into Minnesota's far north.Ely, Minnesota, wilderness guides Dave and Amy Freeman entered the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness on September 23, 2015, and didn’t leave until September 23, 2016, living for 366 continuous days in the wild, without crossing a road or going into a building. Their expedition carried them over 2,000 miles by canoe, foot, ski, snowshoe and dog team over some 500 lakes, rivers and streams, camping at some 120 different places through all four seasons. The pair travelled there in support of the Save the Boundary Waters group, which has fought for years against proposed sulphide ore copper mining near the border of the wilderness, due to fears that mine runoff might damage the watershed's interconnected lakes for generations.A wilderness with robust federal safeguardsThe Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness is a million-plus acres of wilderness in the northern portion of Superior National Forest and extends almost 150 miles along the international boundary with Canada. The US Forest Service manages the land and classified the area as protected wilderness under the Wilderness Act of 1964. Development and motorized activity are therefore restricted within its borders, though traditional non-motorized aids like sailboats, sleds and dog teams remain permitted. That legal protection applies to the wilderness itself, but the watershed that feeds its lakes stretches beyond the boundary line into places where mineral leases have been proposed, which is precisely the gap the Freemans wanted to point out.It wasn’t just camping to live in the outdoors for a full year. The duo fell through ice, were stalked at a distance by wolves, drank directly from the lakes and used a small sailboat and sled to transport supplies between seasons. Even so, they used satellite technology to stay in touch with schools and supporters throughout the year, turning what could have been a private ordeal into a public campaign followed by hundreds of thousands of people online. On the last day, when they eventually paddled out, dozens of canoes and a crowd of well-wishers gathered at Ely to welcome them home.An extension of years spent teaching via travelThe wilderness year was not a one-off adventure but part of a longer pattern in the Freemans’ lives. The couple had already kayaked, canoed, dog-sledded and hiked across North America on a three-year, more than 11,000-mile trek and separately paddled 2,000 miles over 100 days from Minnesota to Washington to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the Wilderness Act. Each of these expeditions was linked to their nonprofit, Wilderness Classroom, which uses the trips to teach literacy, critical thinking and environmental awareness to tens of thousands of school children who follow along remotely, instead of in person.The mix of endurance travel and education brought the pair accolades beyond the campaign itself, including inclusion on National Geographic’s Adventurers of the Year list and a written account of their wilderness year that won a regional book prize. The campaign they supported continued to gain political momentum in the years that followed, with government reviews and leasing decisions around the planned mining sites changing back and forth depending on the administration in office at any given time.They did not write letters or deliver speeches from afar but lived in the landscape they wanted to protect through blizzards, thaws and every season in between, believing that a prolonged presence would be more effective than words. That effort continues to shape the discussion around one of America's most visited wilderness areas, a watershed where the mining fight is still unresolved: federal protections were rolled back by Congress in 2026, even as Minnesota's state government has moved to block new mining leases nearby.You use AI every day. articles.title: What is happening between Twitch streamers KitsuFox and Nosiiree? Breakup drama explained
articles.summary: Twitch streamers KitsuFox and Nosiiree are at the center of a breakup controversy after KitsuFox accused her ex-boyfriend of repeatedly contacting her
articles.body: Twitch streamers KitsuFox and Nosiiree are at the center of a breakup controversy after KitsuFox accused her ex-boyfriend of repeatedly contacting her after their relationship ended. During a September 23 livestream, KitsuFox claimed that Nosiiree kept finding ways to reach her after she blocked him and changed her phone number. She also said he showed up at her door. Nosiiree later responded during his own livestream, denying that he is a stalker. He said he still loves KitsuFox and called their relationship problems personal.What happened between Twitch streamers KitsuFox and Nosiiree?KitsuFox said the main problem started after she and Nosiiree broke up. According to her, she tried to end contact by blocking him and changing her phone number.However, she claimed that Nosiiree continued trying to reach her. KitsuFox said he allegedly used fake phone numbers to contact her. She also claimed that he showed up at her home.During her livestream, KitsuFox asked him to stop coming to her door. She described the situation as a “very bad cycle” that she had tried to leave.KitsuFox also spoke about how she felt during their relationship. She said she believed Nosiiree would have been very angry if she had acted in the same way around other men.She also admitted that the situation was difficult because she still had feelings for him. According to KitsuFox, his attempts to reconnect sometimes made her feel that he did not want to lose her.Why is Nosiiree denying the stalking claims?Nosiiree gave his side of the story during his own livestream on September 23. He directly rejected the accusation and said, “I want to say I'm not a stalker.”He also said there was no hate between them and repeated that he still loved KitsuFox. Nosiiree described KitsuFox as “kind of sensitive when it comes to certain things.”The streamer and rapper also said he did not believe their private relationship problems should have become public. He called the matter “really personal” and said it should have “been kept off the internet.”Nosiiree also said he believed he had done nothing wrong.The two Twitch streamers have now given different accounts of what happened after their breakup. KitsuFox says she tried to cut contact but claims Nosiiree continued reaching out. Nosiiree denies being a stalker and says the dispute is a private matter.For now, the public controversy is based on the two streamers’ own statements from their September 23 livestreams, with both sides presenting different versions of the breakup.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Colorado couple arrived from Mexico in 1995 hoping their three children could build lives beyond the family business; 31 years later, they are closing Los Tarascos because that dream came true
articles.summary: A Colorado couple who moved from Mexico to the US in 1995 with a dream of giving their three children a different future, have closed the restaurant they
articles.body: A Colorado couple who moved from Mexico to the US in 1995 with a dream of giving their three children a different future, have closed the restaurant they built over 31 years. Jose and Maria Caballero shut Los Tarascos in Fort Collins, Colorado, after decades of serving Mexican food to the local community.The restaurant close its doors on Wednesday, AOL reported. For the Caballeros, the closure is not just end of a restaurant. It is about the goal that brought them to Fort Collins in the first place- giving their children the chance to attend college, build careers and have lives outside the family business."My motivation was always my children, to give them a better life," Maria Caballero told the Coloradoan in an interview conducted in Spanish.When the couple arrived from Michoacan, Mexico, they brought their three children, Hugo Caballero Jr, Gema Caballero and Priscilla Umbreit. They knew little English and were starting a business in a new country. Jose already had restaurant experience in Mexico, while Maria had spent much of her life raising their family and was not prepared for the responsibility of helping run a restaurant. "I wasn't prepared for that responsibility," Maria said.Los Tarascos started in a small location, where Thai Station now operates. Jose and Maria worked while raising their children and learning how to manage life in Fort Collins. They cooked recipes from their families in Mexico, including dishes that came from Maria's mother and Jose's family.As more relatives came from Mexico, they also joined the restaurant. Parents, siblings and other family members helped with the business, making Los Tarascos a family operation from its early years.From humble start to popularityBuilding a customer base did not happen immediately. Jose said authentic Mexican food was less common in Fort Collins when the restaurant opened in 1995. Some dishes were adjusted slightly for local tastes, while the family also introduced customers to the flavours they had grown up eating.Over time, customers began bringing friends. The restaurant continued to grow, and after about 13 years in its first location, the Caballeros needed a larger space.That led them to 622 S. College Ave., where Los Tarascos spent most of its 31-year history. Another leap in the restaurant's history came with its longtime customer and local businessman Jim Mokler.When the Caballeros had an opportunity to buy the building, Mokler provided $100,000 to help them secure financing for the purchase. "He believed in us. That was a moment of growth," Jose said.The restaurant's story also became closely connected with the Fort Collins community. Jose said the family could not have continued without the support of local customers. "Without the community, we wouldn't have survived," he said.That support grew as Los Tarascos became a place where local families gathered for birthdays, anniversaries, business celebrations and Cinco de Mayo events. For the Caballeros, those occasions became part of the restaurant's history.Margarita recipe that changed the businessOne of the restaurant's biggest changes came from an idea Jose developed before Los Tarascos opened. He spent months studying successful restaurants and bars and paid particular attention to the margarita programme at Rio Grande Mexican Restaurant.Jose had years of bartending experience in Mexico, so he began developing his own margarita recipes. He tested them and collected feedback from customers before settling on a recipe that became popular."I would sell two gallons of margaritas, maybe. After that, we'd sell eight gallons," Jose recalled. The increase in margarita sales helped the restaurant grow further. "The food was the same. But it changed our life," he said.The restaurant later became a place where customers marked important moments in their lives. Jose recalled weddings, birthdays and anniversaries held there. Some customers even brought the ashes of loved ones who had enjoyed visiting the restaurant."We've celebrated weddings, birthdays, anniversaries," Jose said. "People have even brought the ashes of loved ones who enjoyed coming here."For him, however, the response from customers remained one of the most meaningful parts of running the restaurant. "That's the biggest satisfaction for us as restaurant owners. When people love the food and tell you thank you," Jose said.Adiós to Los TarascosThe decision to close Los Tarascos was not because of business problems, Jose clarified. After more than three decades in the restaurant industry, he and Maria want a slower pace of life. "We still have the passion. We just don't have the energy," Jose said.The closure also comes at a point when the couple believes they have achieved the purpose behind the business. Their children have built lives of their own instead of being tied to the restaurant.Gema runs her own clothing brand, while Hugo is preparing to launch a tequila brand. Priscilla is focused on the next stage of her life after spending years helping manage Los Tarascos."We wanted them to go to college and build their own lives. That was always the dream," Jose said. "We're closing with nostalgia. But we're happy," Maria added.The couple does not plan to stop working altogether. They expect to spend some time helping at La Buena Vida, while also travelling, enjoying retirement and spending more time with their grandchildren.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: US tightens birth tourism crackdown: Rubio announces visa curbs as judge blocks Trump’s latest birthright citizenship bid
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has announced a new visa restriction policy targeting foreign nationals who engage in or facilitate commercial birth
articles.body: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has announced a new visa restriction policy targeting foreign nationals who engage in or facilitate commercial birth tourism, escalating the Trump administration's campaign against arrangements involving travel to the US to give birth and obtain citizenship for a child.The policy, announced on Wednesday, seeks to restrict visa issuance to individuals who knowingly engage in, profit from or facilitate commercial birth tourism. It targets operators of birth-tourism networks, visa “fixers” accused of coaching applicants to commit fraud, foreign medical providers who knowingly facilitate such travel and the fraudulent use of Medicaid, and others who support or enable the practice.The State Department said the measure is being implemented under Section 212(a)(3)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, which allows the secretary of state to determine that an individual's entry would have potentially serious adverse foreign-policy consequences. Certain family members of individuals covered by the restrictions may also be affected, according to the announcement.“Foreign commercial networks specializing in birth tourism have exploited the US immigration system to sell US citizenship for profit,” Rubio said, accusing such networks of advising foreign nationals to misrepresent the purpose of their travel and charging tens of thousands of dollars to arrange births on American soil.“By restricting visa issuance of those who both engage in and profit from this fraud, we are sending a clear message: The United States will not allow foreigners to exploit our immigration system and violate the sanctity of US citizenship,” he said.Court blocks Trump's latest birthright citizenship orderThe announcement comes amid an ongoing legal battle over the Trump administration's efforts to narrow birthright citizenship.On Sept 3, a federal district judge in Maryland blocked the administration from enforcing a new executive order issued by President Donald Trump on Aug 6. The order sought to restrict automatic US citizenship for certain children born in the country, including children whose parents were deemed “alien enemies”, foreign government employees or individuals involved in commercial arrangements to secure a birth in the US.US District Judge Deborah Boardman issued a preliminary injunction in a class-action case brought by immigrant families and advocacy organisations. She held that children covered by the certified class remained citizens at birth under the Supreme Court's earlier ruling.“The Supreme Court has spoken: Children in the certified class are ‘citizens at birth’,” Boardman wrote, according to reporting on the decision. The judge's ruling followed a June Supreme Court decision rejecting the administration's earlier, broader attempt to restrict birthright citizenship.The White House has defended the executive order issued in Aug, arguing that it is consistent with the Supreme Court's interpretation of birthright citizenship. The administration's legal position remains contested in court.The ruling does not invalidate Rubio's separate visa restriction announcement. The two measures involve different legal mechanisms: one concerns the eligibility of certain individuals for visas, while the other concerns whether specified categories of children can receive citizenship at birth.Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force had already revoked over 600 visasThe latest visa policy follows the establishment of a Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force by the State Department in August.According to the department's fact sheet, the task force reviews the activities of visa holders worldwide to identify birth tourism, works to revoke visas of individuals who engage in or facilitate the practice and seeks to dismantle networks that profit from commercial birth tourism.The task force also coordinates information across the State Department and other federal agencies, including the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).The department reported that more than 600 visas had been revoked from foreign nationals worldwide. It said visa revocation action could be taken where there were indications of potential ineligibility, including misrepresentation of the purpose of travel.The task force forms part of the administration's wider efforts to target commercial birth-tourism operations and individuals suspected of facilitating immigration fraud.You use AI every day. articles.title: As Nokia is closing its research hub in China; it is back to the time when Nokia CEO asked Europe: Why you use Huawei, while China has thrown us out
articles.summary: Nokia has confirmed it is winding down its radio technology research and development centre in Hangzhou by the end of 2026, cutting roughly 1,600 jobs and
articles.body: Nokia has confirmed it is winding down its radio technology research and development centre in Hangzhou by the end of 2026, cutting roughly 1,600 jobs and quietly closing the book on a China strategy that has been unravelling for the better part of a decade. Staff were told on Thursday, August 13. The company's explanation was clinical—it is aligning its China operations with how Nokia works globally, and its business there has been shrinking for years. Light Reading reports that Nokia sites in Beijing, Chengdu, Qingdao and Shanghai could follow, though the company hasn't confirmed that.What makes the timing interesting is the argument it revives. In September 2025, at a press conference in Oulu, Finland, Nokia CEO Justin Hotard asked Europe a question it still hasn't properly answered: "Why do we allow high-risk vendors in Europe in our networks," he said, when Nokia holds under 3% share in China? Nokia executives said at the time they had been told European vendors were to be pushed out of China on national security grounds. The Hangzhou shutdown is what that warning looks like on the ground.Nokia's China revenue has more than halved since 2018The numbers explain the exit better than any statement does. Nokia's Greater China sales fell from nearly €2.2 billion in 2018 to €913 million in 2025—a drop of more than 58%. The turn came in 2020, when Nokia lost out on key radio access network contracts with China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom. What looked like a product problem then looks structural now. Danish analyst John Strand put it flatly in January: "China is lost land for vendors like Ericsson and Nokia."Huawei still runs around 60% of Germany's 5G sitesHotard's complaint about asymmetry hasn't aged. Huawei accounts for roughly 59% of Germany's 5G radio sites, according to Strand Consult data cited by the country's interior ministry. Only 13 of the EU's 27 member states had fully or partly adopted the bloc's 5G security toolbox as of 2025. Brussels is now moving to make it mandatory—a shift Hotard called "a very good and important step" in January. Germany wants Chinese components in RAN networks down to 25% by October 1, 2026.Nokia's AI and cloud orders are booming as its RAN business shrinksThe retreat isn't cheap. Nokia raised its 2026 restructuring charge from €250 million to €800 million, with about €350 million tied to China and the integration of Nokia Shanghai Bell, which it bought out fully in December 2025. Headcount, around 103,000 in 2018, should end this year near 70,000.The other half of the story is happier. Second-quarter AI and cloud order intake hit €2.8 billion, up 105% year-on-year, and the stock is up 67% this year. Nokia is betting AI-RAN carries it into 6G. The catch: China is running 5G-Advanced across 330 cities, 12 to 18 months ahead of Western carriers, and Nokia will now build without that data.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Bus ticket destroyed, passenger forced to take another bus; TN transport officials told to pay Rs 60,000
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Perambalur district consumer commission has directed Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation authorities to pay Rs 50,000 compensation and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Perambalur district consumer commission has directed Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation authorities to pay Rs 50,000 compensation and Rs 10,000 costs to a passenger who alleged he was forced off a bus after his ticket was destroyed. The commission found deficiency in service for failing to enquire into his complaint. The order was passed on September 2, 2026.Why did the passenger approach the commission?According to the commission order, the passenger visited Vellore on March 23, 2026, to buy medicines for his son and later boarded a bus to Perambalur. He alleged that he paid Rs 500 for a ticket but was given a Rs 200 ticket, with the conductor promising to return the balance Rs 300 at the destination.During a tea break at Tiruvannamalai, the passenger returned to find another woman occupying his seat. He alleged that after he complained to the time-keeper, the conductor demanded his ticket, chewed it and spat it out. He further alleged that the conductor and driver then left in the bus after throwing out his bag.The passenger then took another bus to Perambalur and spent Rs 136. He sent a legal notice to the corporation's regional and zonal managers on March 24, 2026, seeking the return of Rs 300, Rs 10 lakh compensation, costs and disciplinary action against the conductor and driver.However, the corporation disputed his allegations. It said electronic ticketing machine records showed that no ticket had been issued for travel between Vellore and Perambalur on the date mentioned by him. It also said the actual fare was Rs 212 and not Rs 200, and argued that a photograph of the bus did not prove that he had travelled in it.What did the commission find?The bench of President D Jawahar and members P Thilaka and M Muthukamaran did not accept the passenger's allegation that he was illegally deboarded from the bus, saying the issue could not be decided on his evidence alone in the summary proceedings. However, it found that the corporation authorities had failed to properly enquire into his complaint.The commission noted that the passenger had specifically said the ticket was destroyed during an enquiry before the time-keeper at Tiruvannamalai. It said the corporation should have checked the allegation with the time-keeper or branch manager.“Complainant had stated that he made a complaint before the Time Keeper in Tiruvannamalai bus stand, and during enquiry, his ticket was chewed & destroyed by the 1st opposite party, in the presence of the said Time Keeper. Therefore the 3rd and the 4th opposite parties ought to have got a report from the Time Keeper or from the Branch Manager of the said bus stand, to check the veracity of the allegations made by the complainant,” the commission held.The commission also rejected the corporation's argument that the passenger had no independent witness. It pointed out that the corporation had filed affidavits from the conductor and driver but had not produced a report or supporting affidavit from the time-keeper.“In fact, it is strange to note that the opposite parties are totally silent on this aspect in their written version, and there is not even a denial of this incident. Therefore the objection of the opposite parties that there was no independent witness falls flat. Opposite parties filed affidavits by the 1st and the 2nd opposite parties but failed to get a supporting affidavit / report from the Time Keeper,” the bench added.The commission said the regional and zonal managers had received the passenger's legal notice but did not conduct any enquiry. It also considered documents showing his visit to Vellore and subsequent travel from Tiruvannamalai to Perambalur. The commission said the difference in ticket fare was not enough to reject his complaint without proper enquiry.“Right to be protected against unscrupulous exploitation of consumers is a basic right enshrined in the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, but in the case on hand, it was overlooked without conducting any enquiry. This Commission holds this as a definite deficiency in service on the part of the 3rd and the 4th opposite parties,” it further added.The commission held the regional and zonal managers responsible for deficiency in service. It awarded Rs 50,000 for the passenger's mental agony and Rs 10,000 towards costs. The complaint against the conductor and driver was dismissed.What did the commission order?The Perambalur district consumer commission directed the corporation authorities to:Pay Rs 50,000 as compensation to the passenger.Pay Rs 10,000 towards costs.Make the payment within 45 days from receiving the order copy.Pay 9 percent annual interest on the Rs 60,000 amount from the date of the complaint until realisation if the payment is not made within the stipulated period.The complaint against the conductor and driver was dismissed.

articles.title: Ontario mother of 10 says she received only C$6,300 from a C$19,000 GoFundMe set up by her sister; police later charged the family member with fraud over C$5,000
articles.summary: An Ontario mother of 10 who was seriously injured while helping stranded motorists says she received only about C$6,300 from a GoFundMe campaign that
articles.body: An Ontario mother of 10 who was seriously injured while helping stranded motorists says she received only about C$6,300 from a GoFundMe campaign that raised roughly C$19,000 for her recovery and family. Maryanne Mullett said in an update on her GoFundMe page that her sister, who organised the original fundraiser, received the donations but most of the money did not reach her. Durham Regional Police later confirmed that a family member had been charged with fraud over C$5,000. The allegations have not been proven in court. Mullett's case has since highlighted concerns about how crowdfunding campaigns are organised and who controls the funds raised for people in need.Mother was injured while helping stranded motoristsMullett's ordeal began on January 1, 2026, when she stopped to help people whose vehicle had become stranded near Beaverton, Ontario. According to her account and previous reporting by CityNews, she was trying to help the occupants when another vehicle struck her. She suffered serious injuries and spent months in the hospital recovering.Mullett is a mother of 10 and also runs an Indigenous food business. Her injuries left her unable to work, creating financial difficulties for her household while she underwent treatment and rehabilitation. A family member subsequently created a GoFundMe campaign to help Mullett and her children manage expenses while she recovered. The fundraiser attracted thousands of dollars in donations.Mullett says most of the money did not reach herThe dispute centred on who controlled the original fundraising account. In an update posted on her current GoFundMe page, Mullett said the campaign received C$19,700, but she received only about C$6,300. She said she had initially wanted the fundraiser to be set up in her own name or her mother's name. According to Mullett, her sister instead told her that the campaign needed to be placed in the sister's name and that banking information was required.Mullett later questioned where the remaining money had gone. She said her sister told her that some of the funds had been used to purchase food and supplies for the children. Mullett disputed that explanation, saying she had separately transferred money for food and supplies and that the family had also received gift cards for those expenses. She asked for receipts or other information showing how the money had been spent but did not receive an explanation that accounted for the missing amount.Police later confirmed a fraud chargeThe dispute eventually became a police matter. In April, Durham Regional Police said the allegations were under investigation, but no arrest had yet been made at that stage. By August, however, Durham Regional Police confirmed that an accused had been charged with fraud over C$5,000 in connection with the investigation, according to InnisfilToday. Mullett identified the accused as her sister, who she says organised the original fundraiser. Police did not provide further details because the investigation remained active.The charge is an allegation, and the accused has not been found guilty in court. Mullett described the situation as particularly painful because of the family relationship. In an interview with InnisfilToday after returning home following more than seven months in the hospital, she said she never expected her sister to be involved in the dispute.New fundraiser is now controlled by MullettAfter the original campaign was deactivated, Mullett's supporters encouraged her to establish another fundraiser. The current GoFundMe page is organised by Mullett herself and states that she is the person managing the campaign. The current campaign aims to help her family cope with expenses linked to her recovery. The page says she returned home after months in the hospital but continues to face mobility problems, medical expenses and accessibility needs at home.Mullett has also said that she has been unable to return to her Indigenous food business because of her injuries. Her current fundraiser says money is needed for household expenses, medical needs, home modifications and other costs while she continues her recovery. As of the latest version of the GoFundMe page, the new campaign had raised more than C$26,000 towards a C$40,000 goal.The case raises questions about crowdfundingMullett's experience also became part of a wider discussion about safeguards around online fundraising. CityNews reported in July that police and charity experts were warning donors to verify crowdfunding campaigns before contributing. The report cited Mullett's case alongside a separate Calgary fundraiser that police said was not authorised by the family it claimed to support. Charity lawyer Mark Blumberg told CityNews that people organising crowdfunding campaigns should establish clear arrangements for how donations will be handled. He also advised donors to check the relationship between the organiser and intended recipient and determine who controls withdrawals from the account.For Mullett, the experience has added another challenge to an already difficult recovery. After surviving the January crash and spending months in the hospital, she is now rebuilding her life while dealing with the financial consequences of being unable to work. Her case illustrates why donors and beneficiaries may want to establish clearly who controls a fundraiser, how the money will reach its intended recipient and how donations will be accounted for, particularly when a campaign is organised by someone other than the person receiving the funds.You use AI every day. articles.title: Is PewDiePie done making videos? Here’s the truth behind his latest YouTube announcement
articles.summary: PewDiePie has made fans wonder if he is saying goodbye to YouTube after sharing a new video titled “Thank you and Goodbye.” The 36-year-old creator spoke
articles.body: PewDiePie has made fans wonder if he is saying goodbye to YouTube after sharing a new video titled “Thank you and Goodbye.” The 36-year-old creator spoke about a big change coming to his channel, especially when it comes to his family content. His announcement quickly raised questions about whether he plans to stop making videos completely. However, that is not what PewDiePie said. The YouTuber made it clear that he still loves creating videos and plans to continue doing so, but one part of his content is changing.Is PewDiePie quitting YouTube or just changing his family content?PewDiePie is not quitting YouTube. Instead, he has decided to stop making family vlogs that regularly show his wife, Marzia, and their son, Bjorn.In his latest video, PewDiePie explained that Bjorn is growing up, and he wants his son to have more privacy. He believes Bjorn should be able to decide for himself what parts of his life he wants to share online when he gets older.PewDiePie also talked about his own experience with fame. He said he loves making videos but does not enjoy being famous. Being recognized in public can make normal activities harder because people may stare, secretly take pictures or follow him.The creator said this is one reason he wants to be more careful about sharing Bjorn’s life online.Why is PewDiePie stopping family vlogs after nearly 100 videos?PewDiePie said he does not regret sharing his family life with viewers. The family originally planned to make only one or two videos, but the idea grew much bigger because viewers enjoyed watching their journey.Over time, the family made around 100 videos featuring their life together. However, with Bjorn now growing older, PewDiePie feels this is the right time to change how much of his son’s life is shown online.The family will not completely disappear from the internet. PewDiePie said they may still share some moments from Bjorn’s life, but they will be more careful about what they post.The family has also started using a newsletter, which PewDiePie described as a written version of their vlog. This gives them another way to share updates without showing as much of their private life.PewDiePie moved to Japan with Marzia in 2022, and their son Bjorn was born a year later. The family has since raised him there.PewDiePie is not ending his YouTube career. He plans to keep making videos, but he is saying goodbye to regular family vlogs. His decision mainly comes from wanting Bjorn to have more privacy as he grows up. While fans may see less of the family online, PewDiePie has made it clear that his journey as a creator is not over.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Florida teacher accused of calling 8th-grader ‘misogynist’ over conservative views; Attorney General seeks her dismissal
articles.summary: A Florida teacher has been accused of calling an eighth-grade student a 'misogynist' due to his conservative views. The attorney general seeks her dismissal, claiming potential violations of law and policy after the teacher allegedly pressured the student to defend his political stance in class.
articles.body: A Florida school district is reviewing allegations involving a history teacher accused of repeatedly singling out an eighth-grade student over his conservative views and calling him a “misogynist”.Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier raised the allegations in a letter sent to Sarasota County Schools Superintendent Terry Connor and the school board. The teacher, Liz Ballard, works at Pine View School in Osprey.According to Uthmeier, the student had told Ballard that his parents did not want him taking part in political discussions at school. The attorney general alleges that she nevertheless continued to use him as the “conservative perspective” during classroom debates and pressured him to defend political positions in front of other students.Uthmeier further alleged that Ballard called the student a “misogynist”, circulated the description around the school and questioned his father's influence.“Ms. Ballard singled out this student and, in defiance of his parents’ express instructions, pressured him to defend political positions on demand in front of his classmates,” Uthmeier wrote in the letter.He said the allegations, if established, could amount to violations of Florida law, school board policy and professional standards for educators. Uthmeier has called for Ballard's dismissal and the revocation of her teaching certificate if the claims are substantiated. He has asked the school district to provide an update by October 1.Ballard has disputed the attorney general's account.“What I read in that letter is not accurate at all compared to the actual investigation,” she said, according to reports.The district has not confirmed whether Ballard remains employed at Pine View. Connor said the allegations would be examined through the appropriate process.“Every student deserves a classroom where they feel safe, respected, and free to learn,” Connor said in a statement. “No student should face harassment, humiliation, or retaliation because of their beliefs or their family’s views.”He added that the district would “examine the relevant facts and records, ensure a fair process for all involved, and take appropriate action based on the findings and requirements.”Uthmeier's letter also refers to multiple previous HR investigations involving Ballard that parents initiated. Jason Means, president of the Sarasota Classified Teachers Association, said the investigation involving the teacher had been continuing for several months.Pine View School serves students from grades two through 12 and is a public school for gifted students. The school has received national recognition, including a National Blue Ribbon School designation in 2023.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: SIR row: Congress reaches out to oppn parties to move impeachment motion against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress has reached out to the opposition parties in a bid to convince them to move an impeachment motion against Chief Election Commissioner
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress has reached out to the opposition parties in a bid to convince them to move an impeachment motion against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid the ongoing SIR row, news agency ANI reported citing Congress sources on Thursday."Opposition parties to move impeachment motion notice against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in both Houses of Parliament; Congress has reached out to Opposition parties on the issue. It will be submitted within the next two weeks," the party sources said.Moreover, Congress has directed its state units to organise protest marches to their respective state Election Commission offices on September 25, seeking the arrest and removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The move comes amid the ongoing controversy over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, following a media report that highlighted differences among Election Commission officials over the exercise.The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had repeatedly raised concerns within the three-member poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.While the nationwide exercise has been overseen by all three commissioners, Sandhu and Joshi, according to the report, formally recorded objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months, including four on a single day, over decisions and orders they said were taken or issued without their knowledge.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
